ACTIVE SAFETY FEATURES  
 
3 Brakes
3.4 Braking performance
The braking performance depends upon:
The correct state of maintenance and care of the braking system.
The correct pressure (application) being applied on the brake pedal that ultimately leads to the necessary pressure being transmitted to the brakes. The greater the force applied to the pedal, the greater the pressure that is exerted on the drum shoes or the disc pads of the brakes and therefore the result is more effective braking.
The condition of the tyres and adhesion quality of the tyres onto the road surface.
The condition of the road surface, the speed and the mass of the vehicle and its load.
The proper distribution of brake action on all wheels.
(Página 65 del manual 'Learning to drive')

12 Distances
 
12.2 The braking distance
The braking distance is the distance the vehicle travels from the point at which the driver first applies the brakes, until the vehicle come to a complete stop.
This distance can vary depending on:
The speed of the vehicle at the point the brakes are applied.
The mass of the vehicle and its load.
The technical condition of the vehicle (brakes, tyres, shock absorbers, etc.)
The environmental conditions and the condition of the road surface (snow, rain, state of the surface, etc.)
The driver (psychophysical status –mental and physical state, experience, etc.)
An increase in speed causes the braking distance to increase, but this is at a greater rate than the speed increase.
Thus, when the velocity is doubled the braking distance is four times higher.
(Página 179 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Journeys and defensive and efficient driving
 
12 Technical Improvements that reduce consumption
12.2 The Eco mode
This function optimises fuel consumption. It takes into account all the consumption elements (engine power, gear shifting in automatic vehicles, heating and/or air-conditioning, etc.).
Limiting the acceleration provides a low consumption when driving in urban and peri-urban areas. Limiting the heating and air-conditioning allows saving fuel without hindering thermal comfort.
This provides a more economical and environmentally friendly driving (10% fuel savings in the latest generation diesel engines).
It is switched on and off manually.
(Página 278 del manual 'Learning to drive')
